answer: Under escalating cross-collateral chains, each new identity in the canyon network must borrow one admission token from each of three existing guarantors, who post a ferrous-backed liability bond making them fully liable: if the newcomer is proven fake, all three forfeit their own enrollment instantly. An attacker chaining fakes therefore risks 3^n forfeitures at depth n, so fifty fake identities expose 3^50 compounding loss versus honest timber-camp agents who guarantee at most one stranger and risk nothing, paying only a small refundable deposit instead.
